s1.syndrome_frame: Acute cardiac syndrome with respiratory distress and hemodynamic instability
salient_findings: Severe left ventricular dysfunction on echocardiography
key_facts: Patient in their 20s without noteworthy medical history
Presented with chest pain and dyspnea
Experienced palpitations and symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection 3 days prior
Vital signs: temperature 36.5°C, heart rate 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute, blood pressure 105/70 mm Hg, oxygen saturation 89% on room air
Lost consciousness 20 minutes after arrival with decreased blood pressure
Troponin T elevated at 4.74 μg/L
Pro-brain natriuretic peptide elevated at 4850 pg/mL
C-reactive protein elevated at 18.50 mg/L
Procalcitonin elevated at 39.68 ng/mL
Severe left ventricular dysfunction on transthoracic echocardiography with ejection fraction 38%
Wall motion abnormalities in multiple vascular territories on echocardiography
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

ECG findings: upward QRS complex in lead aVR, pure R wave in leads V1 and V2, sinus tachycardia, low QRS voltage in limb leads, ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, aVF, and V1-V6, ST-segment depression in leads aVR and aVL

Troponin T elevated at 4.74 μg/L

Severe left ventricular dysfunction on transthoracic echocardiography with ejection fraction 38%
Wall motion abnormalities in multiple vascular territories on echocardiography
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

ECG findings: upward QRS complex in lead aVR, pure R wave in leads V1 and V2, sinus tachycardia, low QRS voltage in limb leads, ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, aVF, and V1-V6, ST-segment depression in leads aVR and aVL

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin T, pro-brain natriuretic peptide, and severe left ventricular dysfunction on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Severe left ventricular dysfunction, wall motion abnormalities, and normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin T and ST-segment elevation on ECG, despite normal coronary arteries

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Severe left ventricular dysfunction, wall motion abnormalities, and normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography, with a potential trigger of upper respiratory tract infection

shortlist.label: Giant cell myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe left ventricular dysfunction, elevated inflammatory markers, and a fulminant presentation

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pain, dyspnea, and recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms, along with elevated troponin T, pro-brain natriuretic peptide, C-reactive protein, and procalcitonin, suggests an inflammatory process. The echocardiography findings of severe left ventricular dysfunction and wall motion abnormalities, in the absence of coronary artery disease, further support myocarditis as the most likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While stress cardiomyopathy could explain the left ventricular dysfunction, it does not fully account for the elevated inflammatory markers and the recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: The normal coronary angiography results make acute myocardial infarction less likely, despite the elevated troponin T.

rejected.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy typically presents with a distinct ballooning pattern on echocardiography, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Giant cell myocarditis
rejected.why: Giant cell myocarditis is a rare and more severe form of myocarditis, but the presentation and laboratory findings in this case do not specifically suggest giant cell myocarditis over other forms of myocarditis.
